jobs.title: Geology and Environmental Geosciences, Assistant Professor
jobs.description: The Department of Geology & Environmental Geosciences at Lafayette College invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position beginning July 1, 2027. We seek a teacher-scholar geologist with expertise in tectonics, structural geology, or closely related fields (e.g. geophysics, seismology, etc.) who would create innovative, field-based teaching and research opportunities for undergraduate students. The successful candidate will teach across the curriculum, including developing an introductory-level geology course and upper-level geology courses in structural geology and other areas of their expertise. The teaching load is four courses per year in the first year, and five courses per year thereafter. Applicants must have a strong interest in teaching undergraduates, a record of scholarly productivity, and plans for establishing and maintaining an active research program. Applicants must have a Ph.D. in a relevant field or plans to complete all requirements for a Ph.D. prior to August 15, 2027. Research experience beyond graduate work is preferred and experience teaching undergraduates is a plus. The Department of Geology & Environmental Geosciences is interested in building a culturally diverse intellectual community and strongly encourages candidates from diverse backgrounds and with interest in and/or experience working in collaborative interdisciplinary settings to apply. Located in the Lehigh Valley in eastern Pennsylvania, 70 miles from both New York City and Philadelphia, Lafayette College is a small, private, undergraduate-only liberal arts and engineering institution with significant resources to support faculty members in their teaching and scholarship. The College is committed to fostering a learning community grounded in mutual respect, collaboration, and intellectual engagement. In keeping with its mission, Lafayette provides an educational environment that promotes critical inquiry, personal growth, and responsible citizenship. Faculty, students, and staff share responsibility for creating, maintaining, and developing a learning environment in which difference is valued, equity is sought, and inclusiveness is practiced. Lafayette is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from diverse backgrounds and experiences. Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, a statement of teaching philosophy and interests, a statement of scholarly interests, graduate and undergraduate transcripts, and three confidential letters of reference via Interfolio at the link below. Within the submitted materials, candidates should address how their teaching, scholarship, and/or service will support Lafayette’s mission and values, with specific reference to our commitments to creating a vibrant, diverse, and inclusive community. Review of applications will begin November 16, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. https://apply.interfolio.com/189036 Please direct any questions to the search committee chair, Professor David Sunderlin, at sunderld@lafayette.edu.

jobs.description: Beginning of the main content section.Return to the home pagePrintable Format Job Description - Instructional Faculty in Biostatistics - Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics (25002909) Instructional Faculty in Biostatistics - Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics - (25002909)Description The Temple University Barnett College of Public Health Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics is hiring a non-tenure track instructional faculty member in Biostatistics, and we invite applications for an enthusiastic instructor to teach undergraduate and graduate-level courses in biostatistics starting in the 2026-2027 Academic Year. Instructional faculty teach a combination of in-person and online courses, and the University offers excellent professional development in teaching. Instructional faculty may engage in collaborative research with colleagues and participate in the Department’s Biostatistics Core, which offers comprehensive biostatistical consultation and computational services to researchers in the College of Public Health and throughout Temple University, as well as those in other institutions. Faculty also are expected to contribute meaningfully to campus life through engagement in departmental, college, and university service. Salary and benefits are competitive and commensurate with credentials and experience. QUALIFICATIONS. We seek collegial faculty with an earned doctorate in biostatistics or a related discipline before the start date. Faculty should demonstrate potential for excellence in teaching, and a commitment to creating inclusive, accessible spaces for all students. Because the Department offers courses for students in multiple disciplines (e.g., nursing, kinesiology, health sciences), we prefer candidates experienced in teaching and mentoring students from different backgrounds in an inclusive setting and skilled in teaching quantitative courses to students with a range of aptitudes and using a variety of statistical software (e.g., SAS, R). Online teaching experience also is highly desirable. Rank is at the assistant professor of instruction.THE DEPARTMENT. The Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics combines curiosity with rigorous, applied methods that lead to compelling questions and impactful results to improve public health. This is an excellent opportunity to join a department experiencing growth with research expenditures increasing >80% in the past 5 years and agreements for academic programming and research with international universities. The Department has 15 full-time faculty with expertise in mediation, causal inference, missing data and measurement error, semiparametric regression, latent variable modeling, and psychometrics as well as behavioral and chronic disease epidemiology, cancer prevention and control, environmental and occupational exposures, seroepidemiology and disease modeling, aging and cognitive decline, and cardiovascular disease. The Department annually enrolls over 1,800 undergraduate and graduate students with diverse backgrounds and offers five graduate programs: PhD in Epidemiology; MPH degrees in Epidemiology (in-person and online), Applied Biostatistics, and Environmental Health; and MS in Public Health Data Science. We also administer a graduate certificate in Applied Clinical Research. The Department also contributes to the College’s nationally recognized BS in Public Health and administers a minor in Applied Epidemiology.THE COLLEGE. The Barnett College of Public Health’s mission is to educate, innovate, and transform to bring about healthy, equitable, and thriving communities. Our CEPH-accredited College of Public Health embraces public health in all its disciplinary forms, fostering impactful teaching, scholarship, and interdisciplinary collaborations within and outside the college. jobs.title: Instructor – Computer and Information Sciences
jobs.description: Instructor – Computer and Information Sciences Instructor – Computer and Information Sciences Program The Center for Data & Society at Chestnut Hill College in Philadelphia, PA, invites applications for a full-time non-tenure track faculty position opening at the rank of Instructor in Computer and Information Science (CIS) beginning in the fall of 2027. The position requires teaching beginner-level and upper-level CIS courses emphasizing programming languages, application development, robotics, and artificial intelligence. About Chestnut Hill College Founded by the Sisters of Saint Joseph in 1924, Chestnut Hill College is an independent, Catholic institution rooted in a strong liberal arts tradition that fosters equality through holistic education. Distinguished by its strong mission, collegial environment, and dedication to personalized instruction through a small faculty-to-student ratio, the College promotes the spiritual, academic, social, ethical, and moral development of the whole person. Located in the charming Chestnut Hill neighborhood of Northwest Philadelphia, it serves a culturally diverse student body. The Center for Data & Society is an interdisciplinary departmental grouping of computer, mathematical, and social sciences whose mission is to investigate how data and information can be best used to understand the communities in which we live. The computer science department recently redeveloped its offerings for a Computer & Information Science degree with concentrations in management, programming, application development, interactive design, technology, and artificial intelligence and machine learning. It also contributes to the following interdisciplinary programs: Cybersecurity, Data Science, Business Analytics, and Data Studies for Social Good (DSSG). The program offers courses to prepare students for careers in computer science and related fields. Students take courses introducing them to programming concepts, data structures, artificial intelligence, computer algorithms, computer architecture, robotics, networking, cybersecurity, and project management. The program is committed to recruiting faculty who possess applied experience in Computer Science. We are also committed to creating an environment where a diverse group of capable, inspired individuals interact and collaborate to learn knowledge that may be applied to real work experiences. This position will require an on-campus presence. Requirements: Master’s degree in Computer Science or closely related discipline. Minimum of three years practical experience applying concepts learned in Computer Science. Exhibited evidence of continued professional growth and development. Demonstrates proficiencies in many of the following areas, with a willingness to expand into areas of inexperience: Algorithms Artificial Intelligence Robotics Python, Java, JavaScript, and other programming languages Mobile Application Development Database Management and Security Cloud Computing Systems Analysis and Design Project Management Research Methodologies CompTIA certifications in A+, Network+, Security+, Server+, or Cloud+ are a bonus Strong problem-solving, writing, and oral communication skills. Previous college-level teaching experience is a plus, particularly in junior and senior-level computer science programming courses. Documented experience with learning management systems. Preferably Canvas. Demonstrated understanding of and commitment to the College’s Mission and Core Values, including a shared dedication to inclusive, mission-driven education that supports the development of the whole person. Responsibilities: Teaching 12 credits each academic semester, supporting the undergraduate majors in the CIS program. Advise major and minor students in the program in their academic course selection. Contribute to departmental duties, including program assessment and curriculum development. Candidates who can contribute to that goal are encouraged to identify their strengths or experiences in this area. *** Instructor – MidAtlantic OTI Education Center at Northampton Community College ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ This posting will close on: 12/31/2026 ** No further applications will be accepted on or after this date** ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ About MidAtlantic OTI Education Center: The MidAtlantic OSHA Training Institute (OTI) Education Center is a leading provider of high-quality safety and health training in compliance with OSHA standards. We are committed to equipping professionals with the skills and knowledge needed to promote safe and healthy workplaces. As an authorized OTI Education Center, we deliver a wide range of OSHA courses to workers, employers, and safety professionals across the Mid-Atlantic region. Northampton Community College is a consortium partner with Chesapeake Regions Safety Council. Together we are the MidAtlantic OTI Education Center. MidAtlantic OTI Education Center/NCC is seeking a dynamic and knowledgeable Instructor to join our team. The ideal candidate will have practical experience in occupational safety and health, a passion for adult education, and the ability to engage diverse learners. This role is critical in supporting our mission to deliver impactful, up-to-date training that meets OSHA standards and industry best practices. Customize content to suit the needs of various industries and learners. Facilitate interactive and engaging classroom or virtual learning experiences. Maintain accurate course records and documentation. Stay current on OSHA regulations, industry trends, and adult learning methodologies. Represent the MidAtlantic OTI Education Center in a professional and knowledgeable manner. Qualifications: OSHA Authorized Outreach Trainer (Construction and/or General Industry). Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Environmental Health, or a related field (Master’s preferred). Minimum of 5 years of practical safety and health experience. Prior teaching or training experience preferred, especially with adult learners. Strong presentation, communication, and facilitation skills. Ability to travel to regional training locations (if applicable). Why Join Us? Be part of a respected, mission-driven organization impacting workplace safety. Opportunities for professional development and continuing education. Collaborative team environment with experienced safety professionals. Flexible teaching formats, including virtual and in-person delivery options. How to Apply: Please complete the application in full and submit the following materials to hehritz@northampon.edu. Resume or CV Cover Letter highlighting relevant experience and teaching philosophy Copies of OSHA trainer authorizations and any relevant certifications MidAtlantic OTI Education Center and Northampton Community College is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and students.

jobs.description: Non-Credit Phlebotomy Program Instructor Position Summary The Non-Credit Phlebotomy Instructor is a part-time instructor responsible for teaching all aspects of the phlebotomy training program at Lehigh Carbon Community College. The primary responsibility is to deliver engaging and effective classroom lectures and laboratory instruction, ensuring students develop the necessary skills and knowledge to succeed as entry-level phlebotomists. This role involves comprehensive curriculum delivery, hands-on skills training, student assessment, and fostering a professional and supportive learning environment. Key Responsibilities Instruction: ● Deliver comprehensive instruction on the theory and practice of phlebotomy, including venipuncture, capillary collection, and specimen handling. ● This includes teaching relevant anatomy and physiology, medical terminology, and basic laboratory procedures. Skills Training: ● Supervise and guide students during hands-on practice in a lab setting. ● Demonstrate and ensure students master proper techniques for blood collection, patient identification, infection control, and safety protocols. Curriculum Management: ● Implement and adapt the college’s approved curriculum to meet student learning outcomes and industry standards. Ensure course content aligns with the requirements for national phlebotomy certification exams (e.g., NHA or ASCP). Student Assessment: ● Evaluate student competency through a variety of methods, including practical skills assessments, quizzes, and exams. ● Provide constructive feedback to help students improve their technique and understanding. June 2025 Professionalism: ● Maintain a safe, clean, and organized classroom and lab environment. ● Uphold professional and ethical standards, and model positive and professional patient interaction skills for students. Administration: ● Maintain accurate student records, including attendance, grades, and progress. Student Support: ● Provide academic support and guidance to students. ● Foster a positive learning atmosphere that helps students build confidence and address any anxieties related to performing blood draws. Qualifications Required ● Experience: A minimum of two (2) of recent, hands-on clinical experience as a phlebotomist or in a related healthcare role (e.g., Medical Assistant, RN, LPN). ● Certification: Current and valid phlebotomy certification from a nationally recognized organization such as the National Healthcareer Association (NHA), American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP), or American Society of Phlebotomy Technicians (ASPT). ● Education: High school diploma or equivalent is required; an associate degree or higher in a healthcare-related field is often preferred. ● Skills: Strong communication, instructional, and classroom management skills. The ability to teach and motivate adult learners with varying skill levels is crucial. ● Background Clearances: Must be able to obtain and maintain current PA State Police Criminal Record Check, FBI Background Check, and PA Child Abuse History Clearance. Preferred ● Experience in adult education or workforce training. ● Familiarity with non-credit or continuing education systems. Resumes can be sent to: Isabelle McLeod at mmcleod1@lccc.edu

jobs.description: Position Title: Open Rank, Professional Track Faculty, Accounting Position Type: Full time Location: Holmes Hall Categories: Faculty Exempt Job Summary: Job Duties: The Freeman College of Management at Bucknell University invites applicants for a Professional Track faculty position in accounting, with qualifications to teach undergraduate accounting courses beginning in Fall 2027. Specific areas of need are Financial Accounting, Cost Accounting, or Accounting Information System courses. The initial appointment is for three years, with the possibility of reappointment in subsequent years, contingent upon satisfactory performance. The starting rank will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Professional Track faculty members have a teaching load of six courses per year. Additionally, candidates will be expected to advise students and maintain faculty qualifications consistent with the AACSB accreditation standards. Although this position will not be eligible for tenure, Bucknell values professional track colleagues as full members of the faculty and provides extensive resources to support their growth. This includes access to a robust Teaching & Learning Center and funding for professional development and scholarly engagement. Professional track faculty members are eligible to vote in University and College faculty meetings and serve on faculty committees. Professional Track faculty members are reviewed every three years, with the initial review occurring prior to the third year of the appointment. Excellent teaching is the primary criterion for renewal and promotion. This track includes three successive ranks. Faculty members become eligible for promotion to the next rank after six years of service at their current rank. Prior equivalent service may be applied toward promotion. The Freeman College, an AACSB-accredited unit, offers innovative professional education within one of the nation’s foremost liberal arts universities. We believe that an education that combines technical skills and deep intellectual exploration is the best preparation for thoughtful and capable leaders who will have significant impact on their profession, their community and society. We seek faculty members capable of contributing to this mission. The approximately 1000 students in the Freeman College of Management may choose among five majors offered by highly interdisciplinary departments that combine courses in the various disciplines of management with offerings in the arts, humanities, natural and social sciences, and engineering. For additional information pertaining to our curriculum, go to https://www.bucknell.edu/management . QUALIFICATIONS Candidates must possess a graduate degree or commensurate professional experience in a field appropriate for teaching undergraduate accounting courses such as: Introductory/Intermediate/Advanced Accounting, Cost Accounting, or Accounting Information Systems. Candidates must have either compiled a record of teaching excellence, or demonstrate potential for teaching excellence. APPLICATION Review of applications will begin no later than November 1, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. For additional information, and to apply, please visit Bucknell's career site, careers.bucknell.edu Applications will only be accepted online. We intend to conduct first round interviews remotely. The successful candidate will join the P-MixSwitch project, a collaboration between Susquehanna University and the University of Arizona, investigating the physiological and genetic mechanisms that enable small marine mixoplankton to switch between photosynthetic and predatory lifestyles.The Postdoctoral Scientist will work with investigators and research personnel at both institutions in an interdisciplinary research environment integrating microbial ecology, physiology, molecular biology, and bioinformatics. POSITION SPECIFICS The Department of Architectural Engineering (AE) at The Pennsylvania State University invites applications for one or more full-time, professional-track (non-tenure-line) teaching faculty or Professor of Practice positions in architectural engineering. Priority will be given to faculty candidate(s) in the building construction, mechanical, and/or structural disciplines, with preference for integrative experience. Successful candidate(s) will teach undergraduate courses and, if qualified, graduate courses, advise students, and contribute to the department through service and committee work. Preference will be given to applicants with significant construction industry- and/or design-related U.S. experience, and to those who hold, or are expected to hold by the time of the appointment, a doctoral degree in architectural engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, or a closely related field. Engineers with a master’s degree and significant relevant industry experience are also invited to apply and will be considered for a Professor of Practice position. Candidates should be, or intend to be, licensed as a professional engineer (P.E.) or a certified construction manager (CCM), or similar qualification, and have demonstrated teaching experience through academic courses, professional conference presentations, or related activities. Please see https://policy.psu.edu/policies/ac21 for the definitions of academic ranks and promotion opportunities for non-tenure-line faculty at Penn State. Title and rank will be determined by education, experience, and other qualifications. To apply, please submit a single PDF file (5 MB max) that includes: a one-page cover letter, a curriculum vitae, a two-page statement of teaching, highlighting teaching philosophy, experience, and courses or topics they are interested in teaching, an executive summary of industry work performed, highlighting their roles, responsibilities, and contributions to the projects, or one technical publication, and contact information for three references. System limitations allow for a total of 5 documents (5mb per document) as part of your application. Please combine materials to meet the 5-document limit. Application reviews will begin on April 30th, 2026, and continue until filled, with a preferred start date before fall 2026 classes. jobs.description: The Department of Religious Studies at Lafayette College invites applications for a tenure-track appointment in the study of Judaism at the rank of assistant professor, beginning Fall 2027. The successful candidate will be named the Philip and Muriel Berman Scholar of Jewish Studies and will support the study of Jews, Judaism, and Jewishness in partnership with Lafayette’s interdisciplinary Jewish Studies Program and the Philip and Muriel Berman Center for Jewish Studies. We seek a dynamic scholar whose teaching and research engage Judaism in its historical, cultural, and intellectual diversity, and who situates that work within the broader theoretical and methodological frameworks of Religious Studies. We especially welcome candidates whose scholarship is interdisciplinary, intersecting with fields such as environment and sustainability, digital media and technology, religion and nationalism, materiality and the body, and gender and sexuality. The successful candidate will teach introductory Religious Studies courses and courses in their specialization and will demonstrate the ability to contribute to Jewish Studies and other college interdisciplinary programs. The teaching load is four courses per year in the first year, and five courses per year thereafter. We seek a candidate who demonstrates a strong commitment to undergraduate teaching, an interest in developing a broad range of courses beyond their specific research area, and enthusiasm for program-building, while also contributing to Lafayette’s commitment to a vibrant, diverse, and inclusive community. Applicants must have a Ph.D. in a relevant field or plan to complete all requirements for a Ph.D. before August 15, 2027. Located in the Lehigh Valley in eastern Pennsylvania, 70 miles from both New York City and Philadelphia, Lafayette College is a small, private, undergraduate-only liberal arts and engineering institution with significant resources to support faculty members in their teaching and scholarship. The College is committed to fostering a learning community grounded in mutual respect, collaboration, and intellectual engagement. In keeping with its mission, Lafayette provides an educational environment that promotes critical inquiry, personal growth, and responsible citizenship. Faculty, students, and staff share responsibility for creating, maintaining, and developing a learning environment in which difference is valued, equity is sought, and inclusiveness is practiced. Lafayette is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from diverse backgrounds and experiences. Applications should be submitted to https://apply.interfolio.com/192055. Please submit a cover letter, a curriculum vitae, a statement of teaching philosophy and interests, a statement of scholarly interests, and arrange for three confidential letters of recommendation to be submitted to Interfolio. Within the submitted materials, candidates should address how their teaching, scholarship, and/or service will support Lafayette’s mission and values, with specific reference to our commitments to creating a vibrant, diverse, and inclusive community. Review of applications will begin October 12, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Questions about the position should be directed to Professor Brett Hendrickson, Search Committee Chair and Department Head of Religious Studies, at hendribr@lafayette.edu. jobs.description: The Biology Department at Lycoming College invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor, starting August 2027. This is a unique opportunity for an energetic educator and scholar to help shape a new academic major. Beyond teaching, the successful candidate will guide the acquisition of laboratory teaching and research equipment and assist in designing facilities for the new Exercise Science major, established in 2026. Teaching & Mentorship Responsibilities include Introduction to Exercise Science, Exercise Physiology (300-level), departmental/general education offerings (e.g., courses for non-science majors, First-Year Seminars), and mentoring a diverse student population through coursework, undergraduate research, and capstone experiences. Qualified candidates will have a Ph.D. in Exercise Physiology, Exercise Science, Kinesiology, or a closely related field by the start date. Previous undergraduate teaching experience is strongly preferred. Who We Are Founded in 1812, Lycoming College is one of the nation’s oldest and most respected liberal arts colleges. Today, our community of 1,100 active learners from 22 states/territories and 17 countries comprises a student body that is 32 percent domestic students of the global majority or international. All students work with renowned scholars to craft customized combinations of market-driven majors, minors, and concentrations across our 48+ academic programs. Students compete in 20 NCAA Division III sports, participate in faculty-driven research, thrive in a robust internship program, and study abroad in more than two dozen countries. Lycoming College has one of the highest endowment-per-student ratios in the country, is a member of the Annapolis Group of Liberal Arts Colleges and is recognized by U.S. News & World Report as a top 100 National Liberal Arts College and No. 21 Best Value School. Learn more at www.lycoming.edu. The College proudly celebrates and values the principle of inclusive excellence. In support of its commitment to establishing an inclusive and equitable campus, Lycoming College seeks to recruit faculty and staff of diverse perspectives and experiences.Lycoming College is an equal opportunity employer. To Apply Application files should include: Cover Letter & CV highlighting prior leadership/achievements and vision for growing this new Exercise Science major. Teaching Statement: A description of your teaching philosophy and how it aligns with the mission of Lycoming College, specifically highlighting inclusive excellence. Research Statement: A summary of your research interests and goals for the next five years, explicitly addressing how undergraduates will be meaningfully involved in research. Transcripts: Unofficial graduate and undergraduate transcripts. References: Names and contact information for three professional references (at least one must address teaching abilities). Letters may be requested at a later date. Application Review: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Full consideration will be given to applications received by October 23, 2026. Inquiries may be directed to the Chair of the Search Committee, Dr. Jeff Newman, at newman@lycoming.edu. Visit the Lycoming Biology Department to learn more about our community and programs.

The College of Engineering and the Department seek to grow their capability for research and education in aircraft designed simultaneously in their physical design and in the algorithms controlling them to create new capabilities for Unmanned Aerial Systems. Successful candidates may work at any level of organization, from the molecular to the ecosystem level. The Huck Institutes of the Life Sciences serve as a hub for life sciences research at Penn State, bringing together scientists from across the University to address fundamental questions and societal challenges. jobs.title: Visiting Assistant Professor of Criminal Justice
jobs.description: The Criminal Justice Department at Alvernia University invites applications for a one-year, non-tenure-track Visiting Assistant Professor position for the January 2027 academic year, with the possibility of renewal. The position is housed within the College of Humanities, Education, and Social Sciences. Criminal Justice is one of the university’s longest-standing programs and is supported by strong complementary disciplines, including social work, addictions and mental health treatment, psychology, forensic science, political science, and cybersecurity. The department benefits from robust partnerships with local agencies and a dedicated crime investigation house that supports interprofessional, hands-on simulations. Alvernia prepares both residential undergraduate students and adult learners for a wide range of careers through a strong foundation in theory paired with experiential learning opportunities that develop practical and professional skills. The successful candidate will demonstrate excellence in teaching, strong communication and interpersonal skills, and a record of scholarly engagement appropriate to experience. This position is primarily focused on in-person instruction within the university’s traditional undergraduate program, with an emphasis on active student engagement and presence on campus. Preferred Qualifications and Areas of Interest The College particularly welcomes candidates with: Ability to teach courses such as writing for criminal justice professionals, research methods, corrections, probation and parole, and law enforcement A commitment to developing student-centered programming and experiential learning opportunities Interest in fostering partnerships with community agencies and organizations A demonstrated commitment to mission, diversity, equity, and inclusion Responsibilities The standard teaching load is 4/4. The successful candidate will: Teach in-person undergraduate courses across the curriculum, from introductory to capstone levels Potentially teach a section of the First-Year Search Seminar in the fall semester, as a part of the contractual load Actively contribute to the life of the department through student advising, mentorship, and engagement in co-curricular and extracurricular activities, including career exploration events and partnerships with local agencies Support the department’s strong emphasis on service, community engagement, and student development Eligibility Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Criminal Justice or a closely related field or provide evidence that the degree will be completed by August 15, 2026. Alvernia University is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.description: The Department of Economics at Lycoming College invites applications for a two-year Visiting Assistant Professor of Economics (with the possibility of renewal for a third year) to begin July 1, 2027.The successful candidate will teach Principles of Microeconomics, Intermediate Microeconomics, and a range of upper-level courses relating to their areas of interest and expertise. Preference will be given to those with ability to teach Money and Banking, Environmental Economics, and Financial Economics. However, other specialties will be considered. PhD or ABD required. jobs.title: Workforce Electrician Instructor
jobs.description: Workforce Electrician Instructor Workforce Electrician Instructor Position Summary Position: 15-20 hours per week. The Workforce Electrician Instructor will prepare learners for successful entry into the electrical trades and/or continued academic and apprenticeship pathways. The Instructor will bring significant union electrical experience and a strong commitment to training the next generation of skilled trades professionals. Instructors play a vital role in delivering high-quality instruction that supports student achievement while advancing the College’s mission, values, and commitment to equity, access, and excellence.
